description: Correctness and analysis of sorting, searching and heaps

puzzles.title: \text{Prove insertion sort is correct using a loop invariant}
puzzles.statement: \text{After insertion sort runs on } A[1..n] \text{, the array holds its original elements in sorted order.}

blocks.latex: \text{For } j = 2, \ldots, n \text{, insertion sort sets } \mathit{key} = A[j] \text{, shifts the larger elements of } A[1..j-1] \text{ one place right, and puts } \mathit{key} \text{ in the gap.}
\textbf{Invariant: } \text{at the start of each iteration, } A[1..j-1] \text{ holds the original elements of } A[1..j-1] \text{ in sorted order.}
\textbf{Initialization: } \text{before the first iteration } j = 2 \text{, and } A[1..1] \text{ has one element, so it is sorted.}
\textbf{Maintenance: } \text{the loop moves each element of } A[1..j-1] \text{ that is greater than } \mathit{key} \text{ one place right.}
\mathit{key} \text{ lands after every element } {{op:\leq}} \mathit{key} \text{ and before every element } {{op:>}} \mathit{key} \text{, so } A[1..j] \text{ is sorted.}
\text{No element was added or lost, so } A[1..j] \text{ holds the original elements of } A[1..j] \text{, and increasing } j \text{ keeps the invariant.}
\textbf{Termination: } \text{the loop ends with } j = n + 1.
\text{Putting } j = n + 1 \text{ into the invariant, } A[1..n] \text{ holds the original elements in sorted order.}
\text{Therefore insertion sort correctly sorts } A.

puzzles.title: \text{Prove binary search is correct using a loop invariant}
puzzles.statement: \text{On a sorted array } A[0..n-1] \text{, binary search returns an index of } x \text{ if } x \text{ is in } A \text{, and otherwise reports that } x \text{ is absent.}

blocks.latex: \text{Binary search keeps indices } \mathit{lo} = 0 \text{ and } \mathit{hi} = n - 1 \text{ and loops while } \mathit{lo} \le \mathit{hi}.
\textbf{Invariant: } \text{if } x \text{ is in } A \text{, then } x \text{ is in } A[\mathit{lo}..\mathit{hi}].
\textbf{Initialization: } A[\mathit{lo}..\mathit{hi}] = A[0..n-1] \text{ is the whole array, so the invariant holds.}
\textbf{Maintenance: } \text{let } \mathit{mid} = \lfloor (\mathit{lo} + \mathit{hi}) / 2 \rfloor \text{. If } A[\mathit{mid}] = x \text{, returning } \mathit{mid} \text{ is correct.}

\text{If } x {{op:<}} A[\mathit{mid}] \text{, every element of } A[\mathit{mid}..\mathit{hi}] \text{ is at least } A[\mathit{mid}] > x \text{ because } A \text{ is sorted, so setting } \mathit{hi} = \mathit{mid} - 1 \text{ keeps the invariant.}
\text{Similarly, if } x {{op:>}} A[\mathit{mid}] \text{, setting } \mathit{lo} = \mathit{mid} + 1 \text{ keeps the invariant.}
\textbf{Termination: } \text{the range size } \mathit{hi} - \mathit{lo} + 1 \text{ shrinks every iteration, so the loop ends. If it ends without returning, then } \mathit{lo} > \mathit{hi}.
\text{Then } A[\mathit{lo}..\mathit{hi}] \text{ is empty, so by the invariant } x \text{ is not in } A \text{, and reporting it absent is correct.}

puzzles.title: \text{Prove: a heap with } n \text{ elements has height } \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor
puzzles.displayTitle: Prove: a heap with n elements has height ⌊log₂ n⌋
puzzles.statement: \text{A binary heap with } n \ge 1 \text{ nodes is a complete binary tree. Show that its height is } h = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor.

blocks.latex: \text{Let } h \text{ be the height. In a complete binary tree, levels } 0, 1, \ldots, h - 1 \text{ are full and level } h \text{ has between } 1 \text{ and } 2^h \text{ nodes.}
\text{Level } i \text{ holds } 2^i \text{ nodes when full, so the full levels hold } 1 + 2 + \cdots + 2^{h-1} = 2^h - 1 \text{ nodes.}
\text{With at least one node on level } h \text{, } n {{op:\geq}} (2^h - 1) + 1 = 2^h.
\text{Also, with at most } 2^h \text{ nodes on level } h \text{, } n {{op:\leq}} (2^h - 1) + 2^h = 2^{h+1} - 1 {{op:<}} 2^{h+1}.
\text{So } 2^h \le n < 2^{h+1}.
\text{Taking } \log_2 \text{, which is increasing: } h \le \log_2 n < h + 1.
\text{Since } h \text{ is an integer, } h = \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor.
